newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Deere estimates reviewed.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Deere estimates reviewed.

text.p: -- Dain Bosworth analyst J. Blair Brumley said his 1997 earnings estimates for Deere & Co are under review after the company reported fourth quarter earnings below his estimate.

-- Brumley currently estimates Deere's fiscal 1997 earnings at $3.85 a share, compared with the $3.14 reported in fiscal 1996. For the first quarter, he estimates earnings of $0.70 a share, compared with $0.63.
-- Earlier, Deere reported earnings for the fourth quarter ended October 31 of $0.68 a share, up from $0.57 a year ago, but below Brumley's estimate of $0.91.
-- "The number on its face was not what we expected," Brumley said.

-- The analyst said a $15 million after-tax writeoff for Mexican operations reduced earnings by about $0.05 a share. In addition, a higher than expected tax rate accounted for about $0.04 of the gap between the reported earnings and the estimate.
-- "The one big operational shortfall that was very, very disappointing and was a surprise to us was the commercial and consumer business," Brumley said.

-- Deere, he added, made a significant investment in the fiscal fourth quarter for production and marketing programs new commercial and consumer products for 1997. While the company offered no specifics, Brumley said they likely will be landscaping and related products.
-- "The execution (in the commercial and consumer equipment business) hasn't been what the Street would have liked to see over the last couple of years," he added.
